Profile first.

- Run `pytest --durations=10` to list the slowest tests.
- Run `go test -bench . -benchmem` to find slow Go benchmarks.
- Run `go test -cpuprofile cpu.out -bench .` and inspect `go tool pprof cpu.out`.
- Run `pytest --durations=10 --junitxml=slow.xml` to export timings.

Parallelize.

- Run `pytest -n 4 --dist=loadfile`.
- Run `go test -p 4 ./...`.
- Run `cargo test --test-threads=4`.
- Run `jest --maxWorkers=4`.
- Run `make -j4 test`.

Isolate slow tests.

- Run `pytest -k "not integration"`.
- Run `go test ./internal/...`.
- Run `make unit`.
- Run `pytest --lf` to rerun failures only.
- Run `pytest --co -q` to inspect collection cost.

Replace slow dependencies.

- Replace `time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)` with `sync.WaitGroup` or channel synchronization.
- Replace `http.Get("https://example.com")` with `httptest.NewServer`.
- Replace `pytest` network calls with `responses` or `pytest-mock`.
- Replace `fs.ReadFile("/var/data/large.bin")` with `t.TempDir()` or `memfs`.
- Replace PostgreSQL fixtures with `file::memory:?cache=shared` SQLite.

Reduce setup cost.

- Run `pytest --reuse-db`.
- Run `go test -short`.
- Run `cargo test --test-threads=4`.
- Run `pytest --cache-dir=.pytest_cache`.
- Run `go test ./...` without `-count=1` to use Go test caching.

Use smaller fixtures.

- Use `testdata/users_100.csv` instead of `testdata/users_100000.csv`.
- Use `t.TempDir()` instead of shared `/tmp/testdata`.
- Use `pytest --basetemp=/tmp/pytest` for isolated temp dirs.
- Use `t.Run("case_1")` table-driven tests instead of repeated setup.

Limit expensive features.

- Run `pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing` only in CI.
- Run `go test -coverprofile=coverage.out` only when coverage is needed.
- Run `pytest --timeout=5` to catch hangs.
- Run `pytest -p no:randomly` when random ordering adds overhead.

results.out:
Use this release process:

- Follow repo-specific release config first: `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `Makefile`, `package.json`.
- Cut releases from `main` at a clean commit: `git checkout main && git pull --ff-only`.
- Bump version in `package.json` to `1.2.3`: `npm version 1.2.3 --no-git-tag-version`.
- Update `CHANGELOG.md` with `## [1.2.3] - 2026-06-22`.
- Tag the release: `git tag -a v1.2.3 -m "Release v1.2.3"`.
- Push branch and tag: `git push origin main v1.2.3`.
- Trigger CI on tag: `.github/workflows/release.yml` with `on: push: tags: ['v*']`.
- Publish artifacts: `npm publish --access public --tag latest` or `docker push ghcr.io/org/app:v1.2.3`.
- Create GitHub release: `gh release create v1.2.3 --generate-notes --latest`.
- Verify deployment: `curl -fsS https://api.example.com/healthz | jq -e '.status == "ok"'`.
- Roll back by redeploying previous tag: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/app --namespace prod` after setting image to `ghcr.io/org/app:v1.2.2`.

# Queue backpressure — bounded queues shed load before memory growth
## Evidence
- A 10k msg/s producer into a 1k-slot queue caused p99 enqueue latency to rise from 0.8 ms to 42 ms after 30 s, with 12% rejected messages.
## Next
- Add a bounded queue with configurable high-water mark and emit metrics for queue depth, rejection rate, and producer stall time.
